about: Passages from public-domain almanacs, word for word from the Internet Archive's scans (OCR text). Only line-break hyphens from the scan are rejoined; spelling and OCR slips are left as scanned. collector/build-almanac.mjs checks every passage against the scan's text and fails if one does not match. 'then' is the site's own one-line note tying the passage to a live layer.

thomas1846.title: The Farmer's Almanack, calculated on a new and improved plan, for the year 1846
thomas1846.note: The 54th number of what is now The Old Farmer's Almanac. The Internet Archive dates the item 1793; the title page says 1846.

entries.text: January— 2d, 1845, cold, with snow — 3d, very cold, mer. within 2 deg. of 0 — 17th, rain and hail, which causes the trees to be loaded with ice — 22d, the ice continues to hang on the trees — 27th, very fine and thawy.
entries.then: A Boston weather diary from the winter before publication. Today's weather layers are in Climate.

entries.text: Paper and ink are cheaper than law, and it is less trouble to make a memorandum at the proper time than to leave your plough in the field, to " attend court."
entries.then: From “Home questions for the new year”.

entries.text: The best watering comes from heaven. So, whenever you want to quench your thirst, take the clear nectar from the cool spring. What need of mixtures to allay thirst ? Heaven has furnished sufficient beverage, pure and bracing, for us all ; let us not adulterate it then with poisonous decoctions.
entries.then: The Farmer's Calendar for July 1846. Monthly rainfall and water storage over land, from satellites, are in the Gravity and water layers.

entries.text: Russia is the only country in Europe in which the old style is still adhered to, and the difference between the European and Russian dates is about two weeks.
entries.then: True in 1846; Russia switched in 1918. The clocks on this page run on UTC, which did not exist until 1960.

entries.text: VERMONT. Uncurrent.— Bennington Bank,* Bennington. St. Albans Bank, St. Albans. Closed, &c. — Windsor Bank, Windsor. Essex Bank,* Guildhall. Agricultural Bank, Troy, fraud. Commercial Bank of Vermont, fraud. Green Mountain Bank, fraud. Jefferson County Bank, fraud.
entries.then: From a list of “uncurrent and broken bank bills”: in 1846 a farmer needed a printed list to know which banknotes were worthless. Today's market and currency readings are in Economy.

entries.text: ECLIPSES IN 1846. There will be but two Eclipses this year, and both of the Sun.
entries.then: Where the Moon is right now, and how full, is in Signals.

entries.text: Use legs and have legs. That 's right. If you wish to be in good health, you must bestir yourself, and be on your legs. There never was a better time for it than now.

Fair words make me look to my purse. It used to be said, in old times, that fair and smooth speeches buttered no parsnips ; and I dare venture to hazard a guess, that not a few have found it so in these latter days.

All but one of these six stars is larger than the Sun, and Betelgeuse is so big that, if the Sun were placed at its center, the planets Mercury, Venus and the Earth would have plenty of room to revolve in their present orbits inside the star.
entries.then: Betelgeuse's size had just been measured with an interferometer (1920). Fly to it: it is one of the labeled bright stars in the star view.

entries.text: The nearest known star is a Centauri which, as seen in the Table, is so far away that its light requires 4.4 years to reach us. The great majority of visible stars are distant by more than 500 light years.
entries.then: Still true, almost: Proxima Centauri, found in 1915, is the nearest at 4.24 light-years; the Alpha Centauri pair is at 4.37. “Nearest stars” in the star view lists them with Hipparcos distances.

entries.text: the density of Betelgeuse, being only one-millionth that of the Sun, is only one-thousandth that of air, while that of Kruger 60 is about six times that of water. Betelgeuse is a sphere of highly rarefied gas and Kruger 60 is a ball of matter about as compact as the Earth.
entries.then: From a 1923 table of six stars “chosen as representative of their classes”.

entries.text: A man should never be ashamed to own that he has been in the wrong. It is but saying, “ I am wiser today than yesterday.”
No. 5, a square white flag with a black square in the centre, indicates a cold wave.
entries.then: Weather Bureau storm flags, flown from post offices before radio forecasts. Today's warnings and unusual readings are in Climate.

entries.text: November 11th — Colder, with probable snow flurries. Time to be stocking up with Colgate’s Toilet Articles, always useful and sensible Christmas Gifts. Soaps, Powders, Perfumes.
entries.then: An advertisement written into the weather forecast itself. This page carries no advertising.

entries.text: Mercury will be most favorably situated for being seen about February 23, June 23, and October 14, in the East, just before Sunrise, as Morning Star; and January 13, May 5, September 2, and December 27, in the West, just after Sunset, as Evening Star.
entries.then: Where every planet is right now, computed in your browser, is in the Solar System view.

entries.text: The Spring Tides, or tides having the greatest range, occur near the times of New Moon and Full Moon. The Neap Tides, or tides having the least range, occur near the times of First and Last Quarters of the Moon.
entries.then: Still how tides work. The Moon's phase today is in Signals.
